solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Concerning when brackets support nothing (7)

indicators.note: to bracket something is to enclose it, so AS goes round the rest

blocks.note: as = when ('as I left' = 'when I left'); it splits A…S around the rest

annotation.surface: A dry note on punctuation: brackets that hold up nothing at all.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Brackets' reads as the noun, the punctuation marks; here it is a verb, AS bracketing PROP and O.
annotation.definitionFit: Apropos means concerning or with reference to, as in 'apropos of nothing'.

clue.text: Ancient symbol seen in an evacuated kasbah (4)

indicators.note: an evacuated place has had its contents emptied out, leaving only the shell K…H

blocks.note: KASBAH emptied of its middle ASBA leaves K…H

annotation.surface: A traveller spots an old emblem in a deserted North African citadel.
annotation.walkthrough: The kasbah fits the Egyptian flavour of the answer, which makes the clue feel like a hidden word; it is AN plus the empty shell of KASBAH.
annotation.definitionFit: The ankh is the ancient Egyptian cross with a loop at the top, the symbol of life.

clue.text: Bird coming from tor rose to fly around (7)

indicators.note: letters sent flying around land in a new order

annotation.surface: A bird takes off from a rocky hilltop and circles it.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Fly' belongs so naturally with 'bird' that it is easy to miss as the anagram signal. A tor is a rocky hilltop, as on Dartmoor.
annotation.definitionFit: A rooster is a cock, a male domestic fowl.

clue.text: Correct boards for every game (5)

indicators.note: to board is to go inside, so OK gets on board PER

annotation.surface: A rule that every game should be played on a board.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Boards' looks like the noun, as in board games; it is the verb, OK boarding PER.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: poker is one card game among many, and the surface's 'every game' hides that.

clue.text: Scheming nurses adore surgeon ultimately, not orderly (8)

indicators.note: to nurse is to hold close, so SLY holds the rest
ultimately = at the end, the last letter

blocks.note: sly = scheming, crafty; it splits S…LY

annotation.surface: A plotting nurse dotes on the surgeon, with hospital orderlies nowhere to be seen.
annotation.walkthrough: The hospital scene makes 'nurses' a noun and 'orderly' a hospital porter; both are something else here.
annotation.definitionFit: Slovenly means untidy or careless, the opposite of orderly.

clue.text: Confines of dim space suspect flees (7)

indicators.note: the confines of a thing are its boundaries, its first and last letters
suspect as an adjective means not sound, so the letters are unreliable and rearranged

annotation.surface: A suspect escapes from a small, gloomy cell.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Suspect' reads as the person fleeing; it is the adjective, saying the letters are not to be trusted in their order.
annotation.definitionFit: To decamp is to leave suddenly or secretly, to flee.

clue.text: Dismissal of servant with duke for month (6)

indicators.note: 'duke for month' means D stands in place of M

blocks.note: a menial is a servant doing lowly work

annotation.surface: A servant is sacked, with the duke's say-so, for a month.
annotation.walkthrough: D for duke and M for month are standard abbreviations; swap one for the other in MENIAL.
annotation.definitionFit: Denial is dismissal in the sense of rejecting a claim or accusation.

clue.text: Animal in village initially charges to appear aggressive (9)

indicators.note: initially = the first letters of 'in village'
to take charge of is to hold, so COME holds the rest

blocks.note: to come = to appear ('it came into view'); it splits COM…E
first letters of IN and VILLAGE

annotation.surface: A beast in a village rushes at people, looking ready for a fight.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Charges' sits naturally as an animal attacking, and 'in' looks like the container word; in fact 'in' is fodder for its first letter and 'charges' is the container.
annotation.definitionFit: Combative means eager to fight, aggressive.

clue.text: Smorgasbord — mass dash for one on counter (7)

indicators.note: running counter means running the opposite way

blocks.note: for one = EG (for example), turned round

annotation.surface: A buffet table with a pile of food and a quick rush to the counter.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Counter' conjures a shop or buffet counter; here it means contrary, sending EG backwards.
annotation.definitionFit: A mélange is a mixture, and a smorgasbord is a wide mixed assortment.

clue.text: Sprinkling substance in grass (10)

indicators.note: 'in' reads spatially: one thing placed in another is enclosed by it, so the first piece sits within the second

blocks.note: to grass (British slang) is to inform on someone, to sing to the police; it splits S…ING

annotation.surface: Something sprinkled on a lawn, like seed or fertiliser.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Grass' paints a lawn; it is British slang for informing, which is also to sing.
annotation.definitionFit: A smattering is a small scattered amount, a sprinkling.

clue.text: Cheap floor (9)

definitions.note: 'floor' is a verb; the answer, written as one word, is its noun or adjective form

blocks.note: adjective: a price slashed well below the usual
verb, as in boxing: to put an opponent on the canvas

annotation.walkthrough: 'Floor' looks like a noun paired with 'cheap', as in cheap flooring; it is the verb, to knock down.
annotation.definitionFit: Knockdown means very cheap, and to floor is to knock down.

clue.text: Married at traditional place for ceremony, shunning close island (5)

indicators.note: the close of a word is its end, so the last letter is dropped

blocks.clueFragment: traditional place for ceremony, shunning close

annotation.surface: A couple wed in the traditional way, at the altar, avoiding a registry office nearby.
annotation.walkthrough: 'At' simply glues the surface together; the wordplay is M plus ALTA(R).
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the answer is one particular island, in the Mediterranean south of Sicily.

clue.text: Became opposed to sour commander in street (6,7)

blocks.note: milk that has soured has turned
an aga is an Ottoman commander

annotation.surface: A bad-tempered officer out on the street.
annotation.walkthrough: 'In street' looks like an instruction to put the commander inside something; here 'in' is just more letters. An aga is a title of Ottoman military rank.
annotation.definitionFit: To turn against someone is to become hostile to them.

clue.text: Odd graduate caught hunting wild bears (10)

indicators.note: wild letters run out of order
to bear is to carry, so the anagram carries MA inside it

annotation.surface: A strange college graduate is caught out hunting wild bears.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Wild bears' reads as the quarry, but the phrase splits: 'wild' is the anagram signal and 'bears' means carries inside.
annotation.definitionFit: Unmatching things do not match, like odd socks.

clue.text: In general room trapped by enemy, presumably (8)

indicators.note: RM is trapped inside NO ALLY

blocks.note: an enemy is presumably no ally; it splits NO…ALLY

annotation.surface: A general is cornered in a room by the enemy.
annotation.walkthrough: 'In general' looks like it introduces a military general; it is the phrase meaning usually. 'Presumably' warns that NO ALLY is a guess at 'enemy', not a synonym.
annotation.definitionFit: Normally and in general both mean usually, as a rule.

clue.text: The Spanish children did read regularly about polymath (9)

indicators.note: take letters at regular intervals: dId rEaD gives I, R, A
about = turned round, so the whole string is reversed

annotation.surface: Spanish children read a book about a great thinker.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole string EL TOTS IRA is reversed, so it helps to write it out and read it backwards.
annotation.definitionFit: Aristotle wrote on logic, biology, politics and much else, the model polymath.

clue.text: Avoiding the sides, slid one’s oars straight (6)

indicators.note: each word loses its sides, its first and last letters

annotation.surface: A rower keeps a straight course by keeping the oars clear of the banks.
annotation.walkthrough: The rowing picture makes 'avoiding the sides' a steering instruction; it strips the ends off each of the next three words.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: from Latin linea, a line, so something arranged along a line with no bends.

clue.text: Scary being among last in mine by explosive (8)

indicators.note: the last letter of 'mine'
an explosive blows the letters apart into a new order

annotation.surface: Something frightening lurks in a mine beside the explosives.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Among' and 'by' look like position words; both are anagram fodder, with E from 'mine'.
annotation.definitionFit: A bogeyman is an imaginary monster used to frighten children.

clue.text: Air conditioning enveloping church, it turned very cold (6)

indicators.note: AC envelops, wraps around, the rest
IT turned round becomes TI

blocks.note: AC = air conditioning; it splits A…C

annotation.surface: The church's air conditioning is set so high it has become freezing.
annotation.walkthrough: RC for the Roman Catholic church is a standard abbreviation, alongside CH and CE.
annotation.definitionFit: Arctic, informally, means extremely cold.

clue.text: Very important vineyard of non-professional in retirement (7)

indicators.note: retiring is drawing back, so LAIC goes backwards

blocks.note: a cru is a vineyard, as in premier cru

annotation.surface: A retired amateur's vineyard matters a great deal to them.
annotation.walkthrough: 'In retirement' pictures a pensioner with a vineyard; it sends LAIC backwards.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: from Latin crux, a cross, the point where things are decided and so of the greatest importance.

clue.text: Olympian put in fencing work (8)

indicators.note: fencing a field means putting a fence all round it, so one piece surrounds the other

blocks.note: to pose a question is to put it
taken as written; it splits I…N

annotation.surface: An Olympic athlete is entered in the fencing event.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Olympian' and 'fencing' together suggest the Olympic Games; the Olympian is a god, and fencing is the container.
annotation.definitionFit: Poseidon, god of the sea, is one of the twelve Olympian gods.

clue.text: Stepped up to cover fellow sleeping (7)

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means read from the bottom
to cover something is to lie over and around it, so one piece wraps the other

blocks.note: trod = stepped; reversed, it splits DOR…T

annotation.surface: Someone climbs up to lay a blanket over a man asleep.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Stepped up' reads as a phrasal verb, as in volunteering; it is TROD read upwards.
annotation.definitionFit: Dormant means asleep or inactive.

clue.text: Hard-working person’s code causing damage, unexpectedly (6)

blocks.note: a tireless worker, from the British idiom about working like the defenders of Troy
malware disguised as harmless software, named after the wooden horse

annotation.surface: A diligent programmer's code breaks things without warning.
annotation.walkthrough: The computer virus is named after the Trojan horse, which also did its damage unexpectedly; 'to work like a Trojan' is a British idiom for working very hard.
annotation.definitionFit: A Trojan is a tireless worker, and also malware that hides its harmful purpose.

clue.text: One furnishing shop reportedly is fraudulent type (13)

indicators.note: reportedly = as heard, a sound-alike

blocks.note: someone who fits counters in a shop

annotation.surface: A shop fitter turns out to be a con artist.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Furnishing' has to be read as fitting out with fixtures, which gives the fitter of counters.
annotation.definitionFit: A counterfeiter forges money or goods, a fraudulent type.

clue.text: Beat pounding with good guitar sound? (5)

indicators.note: a pound is an enclosure, so TAN impounds W

blocks.note: to tan someone's hide is to beat them; it splits T…AN

annotation.surface: A pounding beat and a good guitar sound, as at a rock gig.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Beat pounding' sounds like drums; 'pounding' is the container, from a pound as an enclosure.
annotation.definitionFit: A twang is the ringing sound of a plucked string.

clue.text: Type of rodent, it leaves hollow (4)

indicators.note: IT leaves the word, dropping out

annotation.surface: A rodent vacates its burrow.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Leaves' could be a noun, the rodent's bedding; it is the verb, IT departing from CAVITY.
annotation.definitionFit: The cavy is the South American rodent family that includes the guinea pig.

clue.text: Fool contributing to recurrent deltoid injury (5)

indicators.note: the answer contributes part of the letters of 'deltoid injury'
recurrent = running back, so read backwards

annotation.surface: A fool keeps hurting the same shoulder muscle.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Recurrent' pictures an injury that keeps coming back; it means the hidden letters run backwards. The deltoid is the shoulder muscle.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both are everyday insults for a stupid person.

clue.text: Spread with great range avoided by him includes second-rate rice dish (9)

indicators.note: HIM avoids the word, dropping out of it
a set that includes something has it inside, so the outer letters wrap the grade letter

annotation.surface: A mountaineer shuns the great peaks and makes do with a second-rate supper spread.
annotation.walkthrough: The great range is the Himalaya, and HIM appears in the clue as the letters to take away.
annotation.definitionFit: Jambalaya is a Creole dish of rice with meat and seafood.

clue.text: Craft festival with delay returning (7)

indicators.note: going back, so NOEL LAG is read backwards

annotation.surface: A craft fair with a late return.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Craft festival' reads as a craft fair; 'craft' is the definition, a boat.
annotation.definitionFit: A galleon is a large sailing ship, a craft.

clue.text: Reporter’s displaying gallantry on a regular basis (7)

indicators.note: what a reporter says is heard, a sound-alike

annotation.surface: A journalist shows chivalry again and again.
annotation.walkthrough: Knightly and nightly sound the same; the reporter only says the word.
annotation.definitionFit: Something done nightly happens every night, on a regular basis.
